Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:
single Fano generator"):
A(a, b, c) := ‖[a, b, c]‖²   where [a,b,c] = (a·b)·c − a·(b·c)
Unperturbed: [a,b,c] = 2·e_7, A = 4.

variance (from the β document, derivation):
Var(A) ≈ 64 σ²                                (TRUTH)
If the current compiler's stepwise scalar-product rule were applied
instead, it would give:
Var_compiler(A) ≈ 16 σ²                       (COMPILER, 4× low)
This test computes the sample variance of A over N = 100,000 Monte
Carlo samples and compares to the TRUTH formula. It does NOT test the
compiler's variance_of() — that requires the full Knowledge<f64>
chain which introduces unrelated complexities (see ζ buffer bug). The
compiler comparison is deferred to a separate test.
Pass criterion: |MC_var − 64σ²| / 64σ² < 0.05 (5% relative error).
If this passes, β's analytical formula is validated empirically. The
remaining claim — that the compiler produces 16σ² — is then a
separate reading-confirmation task.

within-organ redistribution is instantaneous but Q-transport between
blood and tissue remains rate-limited. The hierarchy is
PBPK28-literature → PBPK14 → 1-state QSS
with monotonically decreasing model-form complexity. Discrepancies

1. Build adjacency matrix (synthetic connectome, 8 nodes)
2. Compute graph Laplacian
3. Extract 7 eigenvectors via deflated power iteration
4. Map eigenvectors to octonion basis (ψ_k ↔ e_k)
5. Compute G₂ 3-form on the eigenvector frame
6. Compute SU(3) branching quality
7. Run null model (random SO(7) rotations)
8. Compare observed vs null → p-value estimate

T3: Null distribution has lower mean |φ| than observed

T5: Associator deviation field computable on extracted frame

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `knowledge_layout_shadows_user_field_name`. A user struct field named `value` was silently clobbered by its sibling. `ir_register_knowledge_layout` preseeds a synthetic `Knowledge` layout — value@0, variance@1, confidence@2 — as entry 0 of the struct layout table,. description: A user struct field named `value` was silently clobbered by its sibling. `ir_register_knowledge_layout` preseeds a synthetic `Knowledge` layout — value@0, variance@1, confidence@2 — as entry 0 of the struct layout table,
comments: A user struct field named `value` was silently clobbered by its sibling.
`ir_register_knowledge_layout` preseeds a synthetic `Knowledge` layout —
value@0, variance@1, confidence@2 — as entry 0 of the struct layout table,
before any user struct is registered. `field_idx_from_name_simple` resolves a
field *name* to a slot by scanning the whole table in order and taking the
first hit in any struct, and that path is what runs whenever the base is not
a typed local: `arr[i].f` reaches it because array locals record a length but
no element type.
So `ext[0].value` resolved to Knowledge's slot 0 — the same slot as `oid` —
and `ext[0].value = val_buf` overwrote the `oid` written just before it. Both
reads then went to slot 0 too, so `value` read back correct while `oid`
returned `value`'s bytes: a silent wrong answer at rc=0, with no diagnostic.
The trigger was the identifier, not the shape. The same program with the
field named `val` was always correct, at any struct size, array length or
index form — which is why size- and index-threshold hypotheses all died.
Guard all three preseeded names. Anything reading its sibling's data here
means the synthetic layout is shadowing user layouts again.
Honest scope: CI runs this suite under souc-stage2, which never carried the
defect, so this file is green either way there — it is the readable witness,
not the guard. The discriminating gate is the `knowledge_field_shadow` case
in tests/madaros/source_to_elf/manifest.tsv, which compiles with Madaros and
was measured red before this fix and green after.

PROVED the identical hole was still live for while/for loop bodies:
var x = measure(1)                        // {s1}
while i<3 { x = x + measure(2); i=i+1 }    // inside: union={s1,s2}
let y = x + x                              // AFTER the loop: union=1

push_scope()/pop_scope() around the loop body discards any env rebind made
inside it, so the reassignment never reached anywhere outside the loop.

checker_check_for_in_expr_inplace with the SAME checker_ns_branch_enter_
inplace (before the body) / checker_merge_ns_reassigned_inplace (after)
pair used for if/match -- they do NOT share a single body-check function
(each is its own top-level expr handler calling
checker_check_opt_block_inplace independently), so both needed their own
wrap. A loop body runs 0+ times and accumulates, so the sound post-loop
value for any Knowledge var reassigned in the body is TOP (widen) --
identical hammer to if/match, deliberately NOT a per-binding fixpoint
union (no such pass exists, or is being added, here).
Two probes below, while and for, each: measure a fresh value, reassign a
pre-loop Knowledge var to it INSIDE the loop body, then read the var again
AFTER the loop (`x + x` / `z + z`) -- the end-to-end proof that the
forced-top value survived past the loop, not just that the merge ran.
Observable only under SOUNIO_NS_TRACE=1: both post-loop unions MUST read
"NS_TRACE union=-1" (top), NOT the pre-loop variable's own original handle.
Per-rule sabotage: SOUNIO_NS_SABOTAGE_JOIN=1 (same knob as if/match)
disables the loop merge too, reproducing the exact fail-open grok-4.6
measured: both post-loop unions revert to the PRE-loop handle instead of
top.

used to take `proof: i64` and compare it to the literal 1, so a hand-typed

`DsepProof` names no `struct { ... }` anywhere in the tree, so no source
text can construct one via a literal, and `types_compatible` (compat.sio)
makes it compatible with nothing but itself. `indep_dsep(1)` therefore
fails the ordinary, structurally-guaranteed argument-type check -- E009,
not a dedicated diagnostic, because there is nothing dedicated to fail:
an i64 can never satisfy this parameter, for any value.
`requires: madaros` because the diagnostic is a genuine engine difference:
lean_single has no comparable opaque-type mechanism and rejects this same
program a different way (E257, a syntactic check over the witness the
compiler itself produced) -- see the lean_single-only sibling file.
